claim: The New York Court of Appeals articulated the "prevailing standard of reasonableness," holding that a restraint is reasonable only if it: (1) is no greater than required to protect the legitimate interest of the employer, (2) does not impose undue hardship on the employee, and (3) is not injurious to the public.
